react_result.final_narrative_text: Two complementary pathway-analysis paradigms — RaMP multi-DB over-representation (ORA) and Mummichog m/z-direct network activity — converge on pyrimidine metabolism as the dominant biological signal in this differential metabolite set. RaMP ORA ranked Pyrimidine catabolism (REACT:R-HSA-73621) first with an FDR of 1.14e-10 and a fold enrichment of 772, driven by four input metabolites: deoxycytidine (KEGG:C00881), dihydrouracil (KEGG:C00429), deoxyuridine (KEGG:C00526), and ureidopropionic acid (KEGG:C02642). The same four metabolites recurred across the top 7 RaMP-ranked pathways (Pyrimidine metabolism WP:WP4022, KEGG:map00240, and three SMPDB disease annotations for dihydropyrimidinase and beta-ureidopropionase deficiencies), indicating that the signal is concentrated in pyrimidine catabolism rather than anabolism. Mummichog independently nominated pyrimidine metabolism as its top hit (p=0.000336) with 13 of 14 pathway members matched, adding CDP (KEGG:C00112) and deoxyribose 1-phosphate (KEGG:C00672) as additional network-matched compounds that participate in nucleotide-sugar metabolism adjacent to the core catabolic module. The pentose phosphate pathway (Mummichog rank 2, p=0.019) captures deoxyribose 1-phosphate and D-glucose as a secondary carbohydrate-metabolism signal. Spironolactone, menadione, methimazole, and 1,2,3-trihydroxybenzene were not captured by either pyrimidine hit, suggesting they are either background differential compounds or act through non-pyrimidine mechanisms.
